name: Faye Tate
life: “I still remember picking up someone's ribbon on a quiet Tuesday.” People around Lighthouse Cove know Faye by a small Sunday habit. Faye takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I take flowers home after they wilt so the family doesn't have to see them wet and gray.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a black overshirt with pearl buttons and a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. Faye has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with short black hair swept back. Faye gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in during a conversation.
personality: Faye treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To remove wilted memorials with family permission.
family: Howard Heller is Faye’s cousin raised in the same household. Faye chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Howard brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The fountain score*, Howard says, “I came prepared to laugh at the performance.”
connections: Cynthia Bloom. Fading flowers and a side-door meal give the family two ways to leave the memorial quietly.

reactions.situation: A memorial is proposed where the survivor walks to work
reactions.response: Faye checks whether the survivor wants to pass the proposed site every day.

reactions.situation: A neighbor offers to pay for a favor that was meant kindly
reactions.response: Faye accepts a small agreed amount if paying lets the neighbor keep their pride.
